slides.title: Drop a pin on North Korea
Howarth RGB app

slide.heading: In this map, lights from 2013 are red, 2003 green and 1993 blue. Why are some lights red?
options: They were lit only in 2013, the latest year

slides.notes: D. Each year is one color channel (Howarth: red 2013, green 2003, blue 1993). A place lit in all three years mixes to white; a place lit only in 2013 shows pure red, so red marks new electrification, for example in China.

slides.title: Daytime images: why and how?
ESA WorldCover

slide.heading: What can daytime images show that night lights cannot?
options: Land cover, such as crops and forests
The brightness of cities at night

slides.notes: A. The other three are all visible in night lights. Daytime images classify land cover (the ESA WorldCover map has 11 classes at 10 m), which matters most in rural areas where there are few lights.
slides.title: What can daytime images show that night lights cannot?
slides.answer: A. Land cover, such as crops and forests

Combining satellite and other data

slide.heading: Which data would you combine with satellite images first?

slides.notes: No right answer. Household surveys are what most studies use to train and validate satellite predictions. In Togo, the government combined satellite images with cell phone data to target emergency cash (BBC, 2021).
slides.title: Which data would you combine with satellite images first?
How satellite images are helping one country hand out cash (BBC)

slide.heading: In the BBC video, which country used satellite images to send emergency cash?

slides.notes: B, Togo. During the pandemic the government searched satellite images for signs of poverty and sent cash through mobile phones (BBC, May 2021).

McKinsey: the disaggregation of development (GIF)

slide.heading: The animation zooms in from one bubble for the whole world. How many micro regions does it end with?

slides.notes: C. The McKinsey Global Institute view (Pixels of Progress) splits the world into more than 40,000 micro regions, a 230 times increase in resolution over countries. Averages hide most of the variation.
